_README: Where the player stands with each of the ten organisations.
WRITTEN BY HAND, like rules.json and playtest_level.json. export_data.py
never overwrites it. The organisations themselves come from the workbook
(boosters.json); this file only says how standing with them works.
EVERY NUMBER IS A PLACEHOLDER awaiting Cameron.
Pleasing an organisation at a press conference - answering a question in
the suit it invites - raises your standing with the group behind that
question by 'per_please'. Standing starts at 'start' for all ten and is
held between levels.
LIVES FOR THIS SITTING ONLY. Like the meta-variables in sanban.json, it
is lost when the game is closed until milestone M4 builds saving.
WHAT STANDING DOES. Cameron's decision: an organisation will not sell you
its backing until you have given it reason to. 'required_standing' is the
standing you need with the organisation behind a modifier before it can
be bought at all - the press conference's long-term payoff.
Override it for a single modifier under 'required_standing_by_modifier',
so a National organisation can ask more than a local one without any of
it becoming a special case in code. PLACEHOLDER NUMBERS.
2026-09-28: 'start' used to be the only lever, so every organisation
opened at the same flat number - a player could not tell one group's
backing from another's on the Backing screen before doing anything at
all. Each organisation can now start somewhere else instead: the
workbook's Boosters tab has its own 'Starting Standing' column
(boosters.json's own 'starting_standing', per booster_id), read by
GameState.reset_booster_standing() before it falls back to the flat
'start' below for any booster that column leaves blank. Filling it in
is a political-characterization call (how warm each real organisation
is to a brand-new legislator) - Cameron's, in the workbook, not a
second number to keep in sync here.
2026-09-28, Cameron: a WEAK-graded answer now annoys the same organisation a
strong one would have pleased, by 'per_displease'. 'question_swing_cap' is a
hard ceiling (both directions) on how far ONE stage's question-answering can
move any single organisation's standing, net of every please/displease it saw
that stage - GameState._apply_question_boosters().
2026-09-29, Cameron: arguing an opponent's own support all the way down to
zero ends the fight for them outright, even short of the win threshold - a
combat instant win (BattleEngine._check_outcome(), 'has_threshold and
state.bar.opponent <= 0'). Whichever organisation that opponent was
affiliated with (opponents.json's own Affiliation column) takes a flat hit,
'instant_win_penalty', applied once per organisation touched this stage
(GameState._apply_instant_win_penalties()) - a separate, simpler mechanic
from the please/displease netting above, since it is never about a
question's own grade.
